references.text: Samson's strength came from the Lord's Spirit, who here also gave him power to perform mighty deeds against the Philistines.
Samson killed a thousand Philistines with an ass's jawbone, illustrating his earlier victories over the Philistines throughout his life.
Samson's prayer to God for strength one last time, which led to his final act of power described in verse 30.
The people rescued Jonathan from death, a contrast to Samson who was willing to die together with his enemies.
Samson is mentioned among the heroes of faith who by faith achieved righteousness and received power to overcome enemies.
Christ was obedient unto death, a self-sacrificing death that Samson's death also was, even though the motives were different.
The grain of wheat that falls into the earth and dies bears much fruit - Samson's death led to greater victory than his life.
